items.summary: 100 entries re-checked on 2 Oct 2026: 6 with new commits, 0 new releases, 0 grade changes; FlyDoom (eganeganegan) returned HTTP 404 again and its record is kept; 51 videos re-checked: all available, 0 removed; 4 entries and 1 video added.

Our own pre-registered body test, Who does the walking?: the FlyGym fly walked 13.9 ± 0.58 mm in 1 s with the real brain (P9 stimulated), 14.15 mm with 3 scrambled brains that sent identical drives, 14.28 mm with a brainless constant drive and 13.96 mm with brainless random drives; the real brain added turning commands (DNa02); sugar sent no walking command (MN9 82 Hz) and the fly stood. The rate-to-drive mapping is ours and caps the drive. One stimulus, one model, one body, 1 s, open loop.

Controls ledger 2026-10-02-run6: 33 studies, 25 with a wiring null (helps 10, no difference 6, worse 2, mixed 6, not yet scored 1); new study byo-flygym-body (no difference, fair, strong; its 3 shuffles sent identical drives). No scoring rule changed; new display-only arm fields activity_ratio and activity_class; stale notes of our fair test fixed at the source; fly-cartpole updated to commit 077dcba (392.5 vs 390.3 steps, p = 0.48).

Gain check of our 1 Oct fair test: x2.5 matched shuffle 3 (10,138 spikes) but shuffles 4 and 5 fired 24,277 and 29,297, so the arm is not matched on 3 shuffles and tuned_equally stays false; MN9 stayed at 0 Hz in all six gain trials (0.37 to 2.12 times the real activity). Our row stays mixed, unfair and weak.

New verdict: "I put a fly's brain into Terraria. And tried to train it" (28,244 views on 2 Oct 2026), grade B: a checksummed MaleCNS v1.0 connectome with reward-modulated plasticity drives a Terraria body through hand-mapped senses and muscles; no control; the code predates the video.
Is it real? gains a Who does the walking? section with our body test as context for embodied claims (Eon, Gorilla Tag, FLY67); it changes no grade. Gorilla Tag re-checked at 623,504 views, still U.

4 new entries: Hidden attractor in the Shiu et al. model (A), Digital Fly in Terraria (B), How much of fly walking is written in the wiring? (B, provisional) and FlyGym + BANC v888 bridge (C, a derivative, not a lure).
1 new video in the gallery: the creator's upload of the Terraria fly (grade B). 52 videos; thumbnails unchanged.

Build your own: the deeper path Add a body is now tested (2 Oct 2026): brain tested, body tested (uv, CPython 3.12.11, flygym 2.1.0, MUJOCO_GL=disable, TMPDIR fix), mapping ours, with commands, pins, expected numbers and the full source.
How it works: a measured who-does-what diagram for a brain driving a body (stimulus, brain, our mapping, body controller).
Sixth research report: our body test, the gain check, the Terraria verdict, tracking, new entries, method and limits.

94 entries re-checked on 1 Oct 2026: 3 with new commits, 0 new releases, 0 grade changes; FlyDoom (eganeganegan) returns HTTP 404 and is kept until a re-check; 49 videos re-checked: all available, 0 removed; 6 entries and 2 videos added.

Our own pre-registered fair test on Does fly wiring help?: real wiring 85.2 ± 3.56 Hz; degree-preserving and weight shuffles 0 Hz (5 each); boundary-preserving 39 ± 1.22 Hz (retention 0.46); sign shuffle 214 ± 43 Hz with the whole brain ignited; gain check 0 Hz at every gain, not matched. One reflex, one model, one trial per shuffle.

Controls ledger: 32 studies, 24 with a wiring null (helps 10, no difference 5, worse 2, mixed 6, not yet scored 1). Our own study row now scores mixed, unfair null and weak method by the fixed rules (30 Sep: helps, partly fair, moderate); new study Brain Runners. controls.json updated.
Is it real?: new verdict on "I Taught a Fly How to Play Gorilla Tag (seriously)" (527,756 views on 1 Oct 2026): grade U, no model, data or code named; video not watched.
Is it real?: new verdict on "I Made Two Real Flies Brain Fight Each other in JJS" (139,364 views): grade U, no code.

New chart: a brainless autopilot plays Doom as well as the fly brain, with all 18 results of the Doom control study's file (DOOMFLY 53.34 s, matched autopilot 51.93 s, best of 12 settings 53.44 s, shuffled wiring 6.75 s); it replaces the earlier Doom bar chart on Is it real? and the DOOMFLY page.
6 new catalogue entries: Brain Runners (A), Doodle Fly (B), FLY67 (B), Fly x Jev (C), and the Gorilla Tag and Roblox fight video claims (U).
2 new videos: the creators' own uploads of the Gorilla Tag and Roblox fight videos (both U), described from their titles and descriptions only.

Build your own re-tested from an empty folder on 1 Oct 2026: pins and data checksums unchanged, 6 tests passed, 82.0 Hz bit-exact with the first run; new box Try a fair control yourself with our shuffle code (wiring it into the beginner files is untested).
Research report of the fifth check: our fair test with its pre-registered design and deviations, the two verdicts, the views-sorted lead scan, tracking, new entries, method and limits.
82 entries re-checked on 30 Sep 2026: 7 with new commits, 3 new releases, 0 grade changes, 0 main-link failures; 47 videos re-checked: all available, 0 removed; 12 entries and 2 videos added.

New page Does fly wiring help?: 31 control studies side by side. Sometimes: real fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 10 of 23 studies, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits; in trained, reservoir and ML tasks it tied or lost (7). The fly network beats a no-brain baseline in only 2 of 13. Only 9 studies are strong; numbers are the authors'.
New data file controls.json with its JSON Schema: every study's arms, source files, retention and rule-based wiring effect, fairness and quality labels.

Is it real?: new verdict on FlyLeno, "Tonight's host: Grey Leno, piloted by Drosophila melanogaster" (grade B, borderline C: the whole FlyWire brain runs untrained, but gait, homing and action choice are engineered and there is no control).

Is it real?: the DOOMFLY row adds the Doom control study's sweep of 12 autopilot settings: the best survives 53.44 s against DOOMFLY's 53.34 s, next to the matched autopilot's 51.93 s. The controls section now points to the 31-study ledger instead of its 20-study table.

Re-checked without change: the Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim (both U), flydoom by mutkuoz (new commits concern a separate variant; stays A) and Haltere (round-6 flights, still no race finish; stays C).

12 new catalogue entries: 2 A (fly-cartpole, flybrain-connectome-benchmark), 5 B (FlyLeno, FlyKart, Open Fly, Fly With Me, Fly-NAF), 2 C (making-fly-play-chess, FlyCNS Tic-Tac-Toe), 1 D (FLYBRAIN Bad Apple x DOOM) and 2 data tools (connectome_interpreter, FlyBrainLab).

New releases re-checked: acamilo-flybrain v0.6.7 (damage reward; stays C), FlyWire annotations Version 3.2.0 (annotation release, not a new connectome) and Kick the Fly 2.13.1 (tests and tooling; stays C).

projects.json and its schema gain two optional fields on every record: controls (wiring-null 22, baseline-only 8, none 64) and wiring_effect; the catalogue filter gains a Controls filter. Additive: no field removed or renamed.
2 new videos: Vinesauce's FlyLeno stream (B), labelled as a streamer's playthrough, not the author's upload, and Fly-NAF's best run (B), the author's upload.
Lead scan: 1 claim promoted (FlyLeno); Leetzerzz's Pokémon stream and the Rainbow Six claim unchanged; 0 link failures and 0 video removals.
Build your own: pins unchanged after a PyPI check (full re-test due by 12 Oct 2026); the Add a body path states that FlyGym 2.1.0 needs Python 3.12 to 3.14 and that brain-body coupling is untested.
Research report of the fourth check: the controls ledger, the FlyLeno verdict, 12 new entries, method and limits.
73 entries re-checked on 29 Sep 2026: 3 with new commits and releases, 1 re-graded (DesktopFly B to C), all main links responding; 44 videos re-checked: all available; 9 entries and 3 videos added.

Is it real?: new verdict on the Raspberry Pi 5 "fly plays Pokémon" Twitch stream (grade U: no code; input read from game memory by the creator's account, unpublished decoder, chat steers learning). The open-source acamilo/flybrain and fly-plays-games (both C) are not the stream's code.

Is it real?: new verdict on "a fly's digital brain plays Rainbow Six Siege" (grade U: nothing published; over 1,000,000 neurons matches no fly connectome; skill would come from training on human gameplay).

DesktopFly re-graded from B (borderline C) to C: neuron rates only switch coded animations, sleep follows idle time and the clock. Verdict row corrected, and a new project page with a download-lure warning.
Is it real?: a new grade A wiring test (fly-brain-zero-shot) shown next to the Doom test: scrambled wiring stops a whole-brain fly steering to targets (2.96 vs 0.34 poles per 10 s).

9 new catalogue entries: 1 A (fly-brain-zero-shot), 4 C (acamilo-flybrain, fly-plays-games, fruitfly-roblox, NeuroWeave), 2 U (the Pokémon stream, the Rainbow Six claim) and 2 data tools (fly-connectome-template, fafbseg).

New releases re-checked: Kick the Fly 2.12.0 (larva brain for headless tests, whose validation fails; stays C), Haltere fast-brain-11 (one full lap, no race finish; stays C) and neuprint-python 0.6.4 (client update).
FlyBrain-HalfLife re-checked: code unchanged at 0ba5548, grade D stands; a second video's claim "There is no scripted game AI" is also contradicted by the code.
3 new videos: the fly-brain-zero-shot wiring test (A), the Roblox maze race (C) and Haltere's Straw Bale race (C).
Research report of the third check: lead scan, two verdicts, the DesktopFly re-grade, 9 new entries, the wiring test and limits.

58 entries re-checked on 28 Sep 2026: 58 unchanged, 0 with new commits, all main links responding; 40 videos re-checked: all available. 0 link problems; 2 dead repositories (fly-survivors, ommatid) excluded. The re-check came about 22 hours after the first pass.

15 new catalogue entries graded from code: 5 A (doom-fly-control, doomfly-rl, Fly Self Driving, flydoom by mutkuoz, a null-model study), 1 B (Fly.exe), 5 C (FlyBridge, fly-api, fly-brain by erojas, Haltere, Kick the Fly), 2 D (FlyBrain-HalfLife, FlyBrain Robot Bridge) and 2 data tools (FlyWire annotations, Virtual Fly Brain).

Is it real?: a third-party control study found that a brainless constant autopilot survives in Doom about as long as DOOMFLY's full-brain simulation (51.9 s vs 53.3 s; shuffled wiring 6.7 s). DOOMFLY stays grade B. New verdict rows for the Half-Life video (grade D: its code builds a synthetic network by default) and the Minecraft farming video (FlyBridge, grade C).
4 new videos in the gallery: the Half-Life video (grade D) and video files from doom-fly-control (A), Fly.exe (B) and flydoom (A).
SWOT's Minecraft farming video now links to its catalogue entry, FlyBridge (grade C).
Text correction: the DOOMFLY limitations text no longer contains internal notes on how its grade was reached; the grade (B) and its reasons are unchanged.
New project pages: DOOMFLY (mechanism, controls, untested run steps) and the Shiu et al. whole-brain model (tested and untested requirements, results, known issues, 17 projects built on it).
Research report of the second check: method, tracking results, new entries, the Doom control study and limits.

New Video gallery: 40 fruit fly brain videos (Doom, Minecraft, Beat Saber, Eon and the lab films), each with its project's evidence grade from the catalogue and what the video does not show. Videos open on their original platform.
First release: 58 fruit fly brain simulation projects, datasets and tools, each with an evidence grade from code, true update dates, licence and link check (28 Sep 2026).

Build your own: a tested beginner guide that runs the fruit fly whole-brain model from an empty folder on 2 CPUs, with exact commands, expected output, a shuffled-wiring control, tests and the full source.
Verdicts on 12 viral fly-brain claims and 13 controlled or negative studies, plus what "91%" and "95%" really mean.
Seven fly connectome datasets compared with data licences (FlyWire is CC BY-NC 4.0) and a reconciliation of the quoted neuron counts.
28 no-install ways to try a fly brain, grouped by what you can do, with honest check labels.
